title: Hexadecimal and Hexatrigesimal Conversion
summary: Given an integer n , square it and convert the result to hexadecimal.
statement: Given an integer n , square it and convert the result to hexadecimal. Then, cube n and convert the result to Hexatrigesimal. Concatenate the hexadecimal and Hexatrigesimal strings in that order.
constraints: Square n and encode the result in uppercase hexadecimal.
Cube n and encode the result in uppercase base 36 using digits then A through Z.
Concatenate the two encodings without a separator.
hints: Use repeated division to convert a nonnegative integer to a chosen base.
Map remainders 0-35 to uppercase digit symbols.
Convert n squared with base 16 and n cubed with base 36.
Concatenate in the required square-then-cube order.
editorial: Concatenate in the required square-then-cube order.

tests.explanation: Thirteen squared is A9 in hexadecimal and cubed is 1P1 in base 36, producing A91P1.
Both powers encode as one, producing 11.
